summary: The culture adaptor is granted read verbs and the other tiers' inputs, and a scope-keyed home-room grant resolves at all.
reason: Internal only, and inert in every default deployment: [culture] enabled ships false, so nothing runs, and nothing reads what it writes (design/culture-tier 02-measurement step 4 is writing-only). Four parts. (1) The wiring defect: RegistryToolSource.build resolved every home room through home_rooms[workspace or ""] while DreamerRuntime.run supplies workspace=None for a scope-keyed adaptor, so a scope-keyed grant looked up home_rooms[""], took the loud closed branch, and every room-scoped verb answered unavailable while the grant read as honoured. A scope-keyed adaptor's key IS a conversation, so its room is an identity rather than a choice and now resolves through a new scope_rooms map built off the same allowlist. An adaptor with no grant still gets the closed, empty-room shape — and that guarantee is now pinned on the scope path too, which no test covered: mutating it survived the whole suite, equivalent only because the one ungranted scope-keyed adaptor declares no tools and returns before a room is built. (2) The culture adaptor now holds nine read verbs (ask_memory, search_memory, about, lookup_person, group_members, where_been, online_now, web_search, web_fetch), all inside the read-only ceiling and none of them an act verb, plus the room's standing position, the note index and the operator's room description as rendered inputs. where_been was in no adaptor's grant at all before this. (3) The account cap is 1,400 characters, down from 8,000, and the character-to-token bridge behind it is now MEASURED rather than assumed: 1.15 output tokens per character (tiktoken o200k_base over a realistic dense-Cantonese account in the objective's own JSON envelope — 1.094 measured, 1.131 for continuous Cantonese prose), against the 1.0 the first draft asserted. 1,400 is 1.89x the objective's worked example (739 characters, extracted; an earlier comment said ~890 and 1.8x and both were wrong) and spends 84% of both the shipped per-completion ceiling and the default loop budget. (4) An account past the cap no longer costs the batch as well. It was discarded, the commit ran empty, the run reported ok and the watermark advanced — so a room whose fold habitually ran long wrote nothing, forever, with only a restart-scoped counter to say so. accept now raises for that one case, which the runtime reports unavailable and which holds the cursor, so the batch is folded again rather than spent; empty and too_many are unchanged and still let it advance. The cap is enforced after the model has emitted and the model is never told it, so this stops the account being LOST, not the long account being written — closing that properly is a change to the objective, which is operator-only.
